will not be ingested.

timeout.description:
Timeout is the maximum time allowed to invoke incident.io. Setting this to 0
does not impose a timeout.

url.description: URL to send POST request to.

enable_update.description: EnableUpdate indicates whether this field should be omitted when updating an existing issue.

template.description: Template is the template string used to render the field.

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

end.description: epoch time in ms

start.description: epoch time in ms

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt is when the key stops working, as a unix timestamp in seconds.
Zero means it never expires; a past timestamp is refused.

name.description:
Name is the key's name: a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters,
digits or hyphens, at most 80 characters. Required.

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt is when the key stops working, as a unix timestamp in seconds.
Zero means it never expires; a past timestamp is refused.

name.description:
Name is the key's new name, under the same rules it was created with.
Required.

query.description: Query is the query text. Required.

queryType.description:
QueryType says which language the query is in — promql or the datastore's
SQL dialect. Required.

excludeStatusCodes.description:
ExcludeStatusCodes are status codes excluded from the score, comma
separated.

serviceName.description: ServiceName is the service the threshold applies to.

threshold.description: Threshold is the satisfied-response time in seconds.

email.description: Email is the key carrying the email; defaults to "email".

groups.description: Groups is the key carrying the group list; defaults to "groups".

name.description: Name is the key carrying the display name; defaults to "name".

role.description: Role is the key carrying the role; defaults to "role".

googleAuthConfig.description: Google is the Google provider's settings, when SSOType is google_auth.

oidcConfig.description: OIDC is the OIDC provider's settings, when SSOType is oidc.

roleMapping.description: RoleMapping maps the provider's groups onto roles for new users.

samlConfig.description: SAML is the SAML provider's settings, when SSOType is saml.

ssoEnabled.description: SSOEnabled turns enforced SSO on for the domain.

ssoType.description: SSOType picks the provider — saml, google_auth or oidc.

invites.description: Invites are the invitations to create; an email may appear only once.

newPassword.description: NewPassword is the password to set.

oldPassword.description:
OldPassword is the current password; the change is refused when it does
not match.

id.description: ID is the dashboard id from the path.

ops.description:
Ops are the JSON Patch operations, applied in order. On the wire this IS the
request body — a bare array, not an object.

from.description: From is the source JSON Pointer for move and copy; ignored otherwise.

op.description: Op is the verb: add, remove, replace, move, copy or test.

path.description:
Path is a JSON Pointer into the postable dashboard, e.g.
/spec/display/name, /spec/panels/<id>, /tags/-.

value.description:
Value is the value to add/replace/test; its type depends on Path. Required
for add, replace and test; ignored otherwise.

generateName.description:
GenerateName derives a fresh unique name from spec.display.name instead of
taking Name.

image.description: Image is an optional cover image reference.

name.description:
Name is the dashboard's unique internal name (a DNS-1123 label). Omit it
with generateName to derive one from the display name.

schemaVersion.description: SchemaVersion is the dashboard schema version; must be the current v6.

spec.description:
Spec is the Perses dashboard spec (display, variables, panels, layouts,
datasources). Its plugin-defined leaves are open JSON, carried verbatim.

tags.description:
Tags are the dashboard's tags; at most ten, and none may use a reserved DSL
key.

id.description: ID is the dashboard id from the path.

query.description: Query is the variable query to evaluate. Required.

variables.description:
Variables are the current values of the other dashboard variables, for
queries that reference them.

order.description: Order is the captured sort direction.

query.description: Query is the captured filter DSL.

sort.description: Sort is the captured sort field.

version.description: Version is the saved-view schema version; must be v1.

data.description: Data is the listing state the view captures.

name.description: Name is the saved view's name; at most 32 characters, no surrounding space.

id.description: ID is the saved view id from the path.

end.description: End is the window end, as epoch nanoseconds. Required.

start.description: Start is the window start, as epoch nanoseconds. Required.

tags.description: Tags narrow the graph to spans matching every condition.

displayName.description: DisplayName is the new display name; empty leaves it unchanged.

role.description:
Role is the legacy role to move to — ADMIN, EDITOR or VIEWER; empty
leaves it unchanged.

aggregations.description: Aggregations are the measures to compute per group. Empty means a count.

filters.description:
Filters narrow the scan; each is a field, an operator (eq, neq, like) and
a value, and they combine with AND.

groupBy.description: GroupBy are the columns to group the rows by.

limit.description: Limit caps how many rows come back.

orderBy.description: OrderBy is the column or aggregation to sort the rows on.

period.description: Period is the window to read, relative to now — 1h, 24h, 7d, 14d, 30d.

project.description: Project is the project to read, as its id. Required.

description.description: Description describes the field, when known.

fieldContext.description:
FieldContext says which plane the field lives on, e.g. attribute,
resource, span.

fieldDataType.description: FieldDataType is the field's type: string, int64, float64 or bool.

name.description: Name is the field's name. Required.

signal.description: Signal is the telemetry signal the field belongs to, e.g. traces.

unit.description: Unit is the field's unit, when known.

domain.description:
Domain narrows the read to one external domain (the domain view requires
it).

end.description: End is the window's end, epoch milliseconds.

endpoint.description: Endpoint narrows the domain view to one endpoint.

filter.description: Filter is an additional predicate in the query-builder filter syntax.

groupBy.description: GroupBy adds grouping columns to the result.

show_ip.description:
ShowIP keeps rows whose domain is a bare IP address; they are dropped
otherwise.

start.description: Start is the window's start, epoch milliseconds.

end_time.description: EndTime is the end of the window, as a millisecond epoch.

start_time.description: StartTime is the start of the window, as a millisecond epoch.

step_end.description: StepEnd is the step the transition runs to, 1-based.

step_start.description:
StepStart is the step the transition runs from, 1-based. Ignored by the
reads that span the whole funnel.

steps.description: Steps are the funnel's steps, in order. At least two are needed.

email.description: Email is the account's address. Required.

orgId.description: OrgID picks the org to sign into when the address belongs to several.

password.description: Password is the account's password. Required.

assignee.description: Assignee is who the issue is assigned to.

id.description: ID is the issue id.

status.description: Status is the new lifecycle state: unresolved, resolved or ignored.

end.description: End is the window end, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

exceptionType.description: ExceptionType narrows to one exception type.

serviceName.description: ServiceName narrows to one reporting service.

start.description: Start is the window start, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

tags.description: Tags narrow the scan to spans carrying the given tag values.

end.description: End is the window end, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

exceptionType.description: ExceptionType narrows to one exception type.

limit.description: Limit caps how many exception groups come back. Required, non-zero.

offset.description: Offset is how many groups to skip.

order.description: Order is the direction: ascending or descending.

orderParam.description: OrderParam is the column to order by, e.g. exceptionCount, lastSeen.

serviceName.description: ServiceName narrows to one reporting service.

start.description: Start is the window start, as a nanosecond epoch spelled as a string.

tags.description: Tags narrow the scan to spans carrying the given tag values.

eventName.description: EventName names the event; required for track events.

eventType.description: EventType is the kind of event — track, identify or group. Required.

rateLimited.description: RateLimited marks an event the reporting client rate-limited.

dataType.description:
DataType is the field's data type, e.g. string, int64, float64, bool.
Required.

index.description:
Index is the index expression to put on the column, e.g. minmax,
set(N), bloom_filter(P), tokenbf_v1(S,H,SEED). Empty keeps the default.

indexGranularity.description: IndexGranularity is the index granularity in rows.

name.description: Name is the field to tune. Required.

selected.description: Selected materializes the field as its own column when true.

type.description: Type is where the field lives: attributes or resources. Required.

field.description: Field is the column to test.

op.description: Op is how to test it: eq, neq or like.

value.description: Value is what to test it against.

dataType.description: DataType is the attribute's value type — string, int64, float64 or bool.

isColumn.description: IsColumn marks an attribute stored as its own column.

isJSON.description: IsJSON marks an attribute read out of a JSON body.

type.description: Type says where the attribute lives — tag or resource.

email.description: Email is the address to mail the reset link to. Required.

frontendBaseURL.description: FrontendBaseURL is the console origin the reset link is built on.

orgId.description: OrgID is the org the address belongs to. Required.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp is when the funnel was created, as a millisecond epoch. Zero
takes the runtime's own clock.

description.description: Description replaces the funnel's description. Empty leaves it as it was.

funnel_id.description: FunnelID is the funnel to update.

funnel_name.description: Name replaces the funnel's name. Empty leaves it as it was.

steps.description:
Steps are the funnel's steps, in order. At least two are needed before
any analytics read will answer.

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when the change was made, as a millisecond epoch.

description.description: Description replaces the funnel's description. Empty leaves it as it was.

funnel_name.description: Name replaces the funnel's name. Empty leaves it as it was.

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when the change was made, as a millisecond epoch.

allowedGroups.description: AllowedGroups, when set, admits only members of these groups.

clientId.description: ClientID is the OAuth application's id.

clientSecret.description: ClientSecret is the OAuth application's secret.

domainToAdminEmail.description:
DomainToAdminEmail maps each Workspace domain to the admin the service
account impersonates; "*" is the fallback.

fetchGroups.description: FetchGroups reads the user's Workspace groups for role mapping.

fetchTransitiveGroupMembership.description:
FetchTransitiveGroupMembership also reads groups held through other
groups.

insecureSkipEmailVerified.description: InsecureSkipEmailVerified admits addresses Google has not verified.

redirectURI.description: RedirectURI is the callback the flow returns to.

cwd.description:
Cwd is where the session is working NOW.

It was write-once — captured at register and never again — which is right
for a run that starts in a directory and stays there, and wrong for a linked
shell, which is a place a person moves around in. The console showed the
directory `hanzo link` happened to be run from and kept showing it after the
shell had walked away, so the field answered "which work is this" with an
answer that was true once. A pointer, so an unchanged path is an omitted
field rather than a repeated write.

target.description: Target re-dispatches a session to a run-target (the #48 association). "" detaches.

terminal.description:
Terminal publishes (or, with "", withdraws) the URL this session's live
terminal can be watched at. A pointer so "absent" and "withdrawn" are
different requests: a session that stops sharing must be able to say so.

actor.description:
Actor is the loop-guard identity the sync writes as. Omitted, the stored actor
stands.

direction.description: Direction is both, pull, push or off. Omitted, the stored direction stands.

id.description: ID is the sync to update, from the path.

trigger.description: Trigger is webhook, poll or manual. Omitted, the stored trigger stands.

id.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

metrics.description: present => a heartbeat; the server stamps its time

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is how much to pay, in cents. Must be positive and can never
exceed the author's pending royalty (accrued minus paid).

id.description: ID is the author to pay, from the path.

method.description:
Method is how it settles: "credits" issues a grant into the author's wallet;
wire, paypal and the like are record-only. Required.

reference.description:
Reference is the operator's external reference for a cash settlement — a wire
confirmation, a PayPal transaction id.

feeds.description:
Feeds is the RSS/Atom feed URLs to read, at most 64. Each must be an
http(s) URL whose host is on the server's allowlist — the SSRF guard is
applied here, at the write, so a stored pipeline can never name a host the
fetcher would refuse. Blank entries are dropped and duplicates collapse.

filters.description:
Filters narrows the merged feed. Terms are trimmed, de-duplicated
case-insensitively, and capped at 64 per axis.

revenueShareBps.description:
RevenueShareBps is the share of net platform revenue a sweep accrues into the
reserve fund, in basis points. 0–10000; 2000 (20%) is the platform default.

autoScale.description: AutoScale turns the provider's cluster autoscaler on for this pool.

clusterId.description: ClusterID is the cluster to add the pool to, from the URL path.

count.description: Count is how many nodes the pool starts with.

minNodes.description:
MinNodes and MaxNodes bound the autoscaler; they are ignored unless
AutoScale is set.

name.description: Name is the pool's name.

provider.description:
Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on (e.g. "digitalocean"). Required —
Visor routes the create by it. Accepted from the body or ?provider=.

size.description: Size is the provider size slug for each node (e.g. "s-4vcpu-8gb").

clusterId.description: ClusterID and PoolID address the pool, from the URL path.

count.description:
Count is the node count to scale TO — an absolute target, not a delta, and
never negative.

provider.description: Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on. Required; body or ?provider=.

app.description: App is the parent application's slug, from the path.

branch.description: Branch is the branch to preview; defaults to the parent app's branch.

image.description:
Image is the already-built image ref to deploy. Required — a preview never
builds.

project.description: Project is the project the parent application lives under, from the path.

description.description: Description is the board's free-form blurb, at most 32768 characters.

key.description: Key is the project to update, from the path.

name.description: Name is the project's display name. Non-empty, at most 256 characters.

id.description: ID is the queued deployment to complete, from the path.

keys.description:
Keys is the manifest CI just uploaded, RELATIVE to the deployment prefix. It
is what replaces `aws s3 sync --delete`: an upload grant authorizes writes
only, so CI cannot remove a file, and cloud reconciles the prefix against
this list instead (grant.go). Omit it and nothing is deleted — the prefix
only grows, which is the old pre-grant behaviour and a safe default.

slug.description: Slug is the project the deployment belongs to, from the path.

status.description: live | error

analytics.description:
Analytics is the opt-OUT for the wired-by-default analytics beacon: absent
(nil) ⇒ ON (the default); explicit false ⇒ off. A pointer so "unset" is
distinguishable from "false" — the only way to turn the default off.

upstream.description:
Upstream/License credit the third-party work this project was published
from. Taken from any caller: disclaiming authorship can only cost the
publisher credit, so it needs no gate (see Project.Upstream).

visibility.description:
Visibility is "public" (the default when absent) or "private". Publishing
publicly is ungated — that is the point of a community. Going PRIVATE is
the paid feature, so an unfunded org asking for it is refused rather than
silently downgraded (see resolve).

domains.description:
Domains are the custom hostnames to attach, in order. An empty list is a
400 rather than a clear — releasing a host is its own call.

slug.description: Slug is the site the hosts attach to, from the path.

name.description: target project name (optional; defaults to the parent's title)

slug.description: parent slug to fork — catalog template or published project (required)

target.description:
Target overrides the derived project slug (optional; defaults to the
parent slug). Kept distinct from Slug so callers can rename on fork.

variant.description:
Variant picks a template's format/page/theme (optional; defaults to the
template's first shape). This is the axis the catalog used to spend
sibling slugs on, so it is expressed here, where the user's preference is.

slug.description: Slug is the site to publish, from the path.

source.description:
Source is the build output to promote, as a path RELATIVE to your org's own
storage space — never a URL and never a bucket. The org segment is prepended
server-side from the validated principal, so the worst a hostile source can
address is something your own org already owns.

hidden.description:
Hidden is MODERATION, and the only admin-gated field on this body: it pulls
a public project out of the catalogue from admin.hanzo.ai without editing
the publisher's own visibility choice, so un-hiding restores exactly what
they asked for. A tenant sending it is ignored.

slug.description:
Slug is the project to update, from the path. The URL is the addressing
authority — a `slug` in the body cannot move the write to another project.

upstream.description:
Upstream/License credit the third-party work this app was published from —
settable after the fact, because the demos that need crediting most are the
ones already live. Pointers so "" clears a credit and absent leaves it.

visibility.description:
Visibility flips an existing project between "public" and "private". Same
ONE rule as at create: public is free, private needs a paid plan.

active.description: Active is the master switch: false parks the offer without deleting it.

end.description: End is when the offer closes (RFC3339).

plans.description: Plans are the plan ids the offer applies to.

start.description: Start is when the offer opens (RFC3339).

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

deploymentId.description:
DeploymentID promotes that deployment's exact built image. One of this and
Tag is required.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

tag.description: Tag promotes an image tag, resolved the same way a deploy resolves one.

labels.description: Labels is free-form taxonomy, each up to 64 characters, capped at 32 entries.

name.description:
Name is the org-unique handle AND the URL segment the prompt is addressed by:
1-64 characters matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$. "metrics", "new" and
"catalog" are reserved. A name that already exists appends a new version.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the template body, capped at 64 KiB. It holds template text only —
never a secret.

tags.description: Tags is free-form taxonomy under the same bounds as Labels.

type.description: Type labels the template's kind; defaults to "text".

name.description: Name is the provider the overlay belongs to, from the URL.

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

description.description: Description is the browse-card blurb, max 4096 characters.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

framework.description: Framework is the stack the kit is built on ("Next.js 14").

preview.description: Preview is the still image the browse card renders, max 4096 characters.

slug.description: Slug is the kit's identity — lowercase alphanumeric with dashes, max 40.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

category.description: Category groups the listing in the shop window.

description.description: Description is the long copy, clipped at 4096 characters.

price.description:
Price is the per-call price as a decimal USD string, exact to 18 places —
"0.0025" is a quarter of a cent and stays one. Empty or "0" (the default)
publishes it free; any positive price makes the listing monetized and
requires Recipient.

public.description: Public makes the listing discoverable by other orgs. Private otherwise.

recipient.description:
Recipient is the seller's payout wallet ID, in the publishing org — the
wallet x402 pays. Required for a monetized listing.

title.description: Title is the shop-window name, 1-200 characters. Required.

tool.description:
Tool is the registry name of the capability being offered. It must already
resolve in the publisher's own scope — there are no phantom listings.

files.description: Files purges exactly the listed URLs — at most 30, Cloudflare's per-request cap.

purge_everything.description: Everything drops the zone's entire edge cache.

zone.description: Zone is the 32-hex Cloudflare zone id, from the path.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, carried per Encoding.

path.description: Path is repo-relative. Absolute or traversing paths are refused.

branch.description:
Branch to advance; empty means "main". A fresh branch that is the repo's
first also becomes HEAD.

files.description:
Files are added to or overwritten on the branch tip — files already there
and not listed SURVIVE. At least one, at most 5000, 32 MiB each.

message.description: Message is the commit message; empty gets a generated one.

name.description:
Name is the repo to push into, from the :name path segment. It is CREATED
on first push if it does not exist.

id.description: ID is the affiliate whose direct rate moves, from the path.

account.description: Account is the provider-side account the sample belongs to.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the window's cached-prompt-token count.

confidence.description: Confidence says how real the counters are, as the meter graded itself.

costCents.description: CostCents is the window's spend in cents, as the provider's meter states it.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the window's spend cap in cents, when the meter knows one.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO currency the cost fields are stated in.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is the window's prompt-token count.

kind.description: Kind is subscription or apikey; anything else is refused.

lane.description: Lane names the meter's own lane label for this measurement.

machine.description: Machine is the machine the collector observed the account on. Required.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is the window's completion-token count.

plan.description: Plan is the provider plan label the account is on.

provider.description: Provider is the AI provider whose meter reported this sample. Required.

requests.description: Requests is the window's request count.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when the window resets, RFC 3339, bounded.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a sample the collector derived rather than observed.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total token count.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, clamped 0..100.

window.description:
Window is the window class, one of 6h, day, week, month; anything else is
refused rather than silently reclassified.

windowMinutes.description: WindowMinutes is the window's length as the meter reported it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC 3339, bounded to a
sane interval around now.

publicKey.description:
PublicKey is one OpenSSH authorized-key line ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA… you@host").
Required; a line that does not parse is refused and never stored.

title.description:
Title labels the key in the console. Max 256 chars; when omitted the
comment on the key line is used.

host.description: Execution context — where this session runs (all optional).

project.description:
The readable build (provenance.go): which product this session builds, and
whether its story may be read by the world.

provider.description: Account tag — the linked AI account this session ran under (login manager).

terminal.description:
Terminal is the URL this session's live terminal is published at, so the
console can watch it. Optional — a session that publishes nothing is still
a session.

image.description: Image is the repository name inside the org's namespace (e.g. "cloud").

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

description.description: Description is the browse-card blurb, max 4096 characters.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

framework.description: Framework is the stack the kit is built on ("Next.js 14").

preview.description: Preview is the still image the browse card renders, max 4096 characters.

slug.description: Slug is the kit to replace, from the path.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required on every sample.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

provider.description:
Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required
on every sample.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339.

samples.description:
Samples is the batch form: every lane a poller measured, in one call. When
it is non-empty the top-level sample fields are ignored.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. This is how a
backfill states WHICH window it measured; the server always owns the
observation clock, so there is no timestamp field.

branch.description:
Branch, CommitSha and Diffstat describe what the run produced; Error is the
failure when OK is false. Each is clamped, never rejected.

id.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

ok.description: OK is whether the run succeeded; Changed whether it produced any commit.

runId.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

app.description: App is the service's CR name, from the path. It must be a DNS-1123 label.

env.description:
Env is REQUIRED and must be main, test or dev. A bare call does not default
to production, which is what closes the fat-finger and confused-deputy
hazard.

It carries no `validate:"required"`: the handler already refuses an empty env
with the sentence that names the three values, and a validator tag would
replace that sentence with a generic one. The requirement is stated here and
enforced there, once.

address.description:
Address is one of YOUR organisation's own published values (GET
/v1/risk/state reports them, and a search reports the one it fitted for you).
An address your organisation has not published is NOT FOUND — including one
another organisation published, because an address names a value and never
authorises reading it.

live.description:
Live turns the model out of shadow. It defaults to FALSE on every call, so
going live is always an explicit act and never a side effect of changing a
number.

Setting it requires an ADMIN of this organisation. Arming decides whether the
model may change an outcome at all — a payment frozen, a grant refused — for
every customer this organisation has, which is a governance act rather than a
tuning one. Stating the appetite and the sample needs no admin.

review.description:
Review is the share of the stream that may be sent for examination, in
(0, 0.5]. The alert threshold is derived from it as a quantile of the scores
actually observed, so the level is governed rather than tuned.

sample.description:
Sample is the share of below-the-line events retained for review, in
[0, 1]. It is the instrument that measures what the model missed; there are
no labels, so nothing else can.

cuts.description:
Cuts are the two RFC 3339 instants dividing train | val | test. Omit them to
take 70% and 85% of the window by time. Splitting is TEMPORAL and then
grouped by subject — a random split puts one device on both sides of the
line and the model memorises the entity instead of the behaviour.

dims.description:
Dims are the coordinates to carry, by published name. Empty takes the whole
surface. They are stored in the plane's own order, never the order given, so
two requests naming the same dims produce identical rows.

from.description:
From and To bound the event window, half-open, RFC 3339. The window may not
be longer than the source's own retention: past that, its older half is
already gone and the dataset would silently be shorter than it says.

horizon.description:
Horizon is how many days a row must have aged before it may be admitted. It
is what keeps a fact that was not yet knowable at scoring time out of a
training set: a chargeback lands 30 to 120 days after the transaction it
condemns, so 120 for the payment lane and 14 for signup abuse. Zero admits
the whole window and is honest only where the outcome is immediate.

kind.description:
Kind narrows to one subject kind — person, session or account. Empty takes
every kind.

name.description:
Name identifies the dataset across its versions: lower-case letters, digits
and hyphens, starting with a letter.

rows.description: Rows caps the materialisation. Zero takes the plane's own bound.

seed.description:
Seed decides WHICH subjects are admitted when the window holds more rows
than the cap allows. It is recorded on the version, so a capped dataset is
reproducible rather than being whichever rows the store returned first.
Omit it to seed from the dataset's name.

before.description:
Before disposes of assertions WRITTEN before this instant, RFC 3339. It is
measured against the server clock at the write and not against the event
or observation times, both of which the asserting caller supplies — a
tenant that could back-date could delete a compliance record on demand.

at.description:
At is when it happened, RFC 3339. Empty means now. It must sit inside the
thirty-day window the aggregates keep and no more than two minutes ahead of
this plane's clock; anything outside that is REFUSED rather than quietly
accepted, because a future timestamp moves the aggregates' leading edge and
leaves every later event for that subject reading as though it never
happened. History older than the window is folded in from your own event
surface, not through this door.

device.description:
Device is the device fingerprint, if any. It is the axis that surfaces
several nominally unrelated subjects acting as one.

id.description:
ID is the caller's own stable identifier for the event. It selects the
below-the-line review sample by hash, so a counter would make the sample
steerable — use the id the event already has.

kind.description:
Kind is whose behaviour this is: person, session or account. It namespaces
the subject, so a person and an account that share an identifier stay two
subjects.

nano.description:
Nano is the value moved, in nano-USD. Omit it for an event that moves no
money: the value features then read BLIND rather than being told the amount
was zero, and the difference is reported on the model state.

peer.description:
Peer is the counterparty, if any. It is an aggregation axis of its own —
"unfamiliar" is a fact about a relationship and not about either party.

subject.description: Subject is the identifier on that kind.

hold.description:
Hold is the state to put them in: true places the hold, false releases it.
One op both ways, because a hold that can be placed and not released pins a
compliance record past every retention boundary with nothing able to let it
go — and an operator who cannot release a hold stops placing them.

ids.description:
IDs are the content digests of the records, as returned by the write and
by the read. They name records in THIS tenant's plane; an id belonging to
anybody else names nothing here, because the statement runs against this
tenant's own file and there is no other file it could reach.

at.description: At is when the judged event happened, RFC 3339.

confidence.description:
Confidence in [0,1]. A processor chargeback is 1; an analyst's hunch is
not. It breaks a tie WITHIN a precedence rank and can never lift a weak
source above a strong one — otherwise every caller would send 1.

A litigation hold is NOT a field here. It is a fact about the record and
not about the world, so it is not part of what was asserted, it is not in
the content digest, and it has its own op — which is also the only way one
can be released. Carried here it was silently a no-op on any record that
already existed: the digest was the same, the insert was ignored, and the
caller was told `duplicate` while the hold it asked for was never placed.

disposition.description:
Disposition is productive, unproductive, or empty for an explicit
unjudged — the AML engine's own vocabulary, verbatim.

evidence.description:
Evidence points at the record this conclusion came from: a dispute id, a
case id, a decision id. Required, because a label with no evidence cannot
be defended when the adverse action it fed is challenged.

kind.description:
Kind is what the subject is: account, agent, merchant, payout, person,
session or transaction. Closed, because a typo in an open field would shard
a tenant's labels into a partition nothing reads and nothing would say so.

seen.description:
Seen is when this assertion became KNOWABLE, RFC 3339. It is required and
it is not At: a chargeback lands 30 to 120 days after the transaction it
judges, and a training set joined on At alone knows the future. Everything
this plane does to prevent leakage is computed from Seen.

source.description:
Source is who asserted: chargeoff, dispute, case, refund, review or
sample. It is the primary term of the precedence rule, so it is closed —
an unknown source has no rank and a conflict with it could not be resolved.

subject.description: Subject identifies the thing being judged, in the tenant's own namespace.

labels.description:
Labels is the batch. Each member is judged on its own: one refusal does
not discard the rest, because a webhook redelivering five disputes must
not lose four of them to one malformed fifth.

events.description:
Events are the things that happened, oldest first. An empty batch is
refused: learning nothing is not an operation.

horizon.description:
Horizon is how many days an event must age before it may be resolved at
all, and it is the whole of the no-leakage rule. 120 for the payment lane
(past the Visa and Mastercard dispute windows), 14 for signup abuse.
Unstated takes 120.

now.description:
Now moves the observation instant BACKWARDS, RFC 3339. It exists so a
BACKTEST can resolve labels as the plane stood at a past moment; without it,
every backtest would score a model against knowledge that arrived after the
decision it is being scored on. An instant after the server clock is
refused: a backtest resolves the past, and a future one would declare
unmatured events matured and hand a training set negatives for rows whose
chargeback has not had time to arrive.

subjects.description:
Subjects are the exact events being judged. Each carries its own event
time, because the as-of that keeps the future out is derived from that
instant plus the horizon — one as-of over a whole batch would give a
January row six extra months of hindsight.

One entry per DISTINCT (kind, subject, at): naming an event twice answers
once, because an event resolved twice would list its own winner as a
contrary claim and would hand a materialiser duplicate training rows.

event.description:
Event is the thing to judge. It is judged against the caller's OWN model
and nothing is learned from it.

days.description:
Days is how much of the organisation's own history to replay, 1 to 400.
Zero takes thirty.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

deploymentId.description:
DeploymentID is the deployment to redeploy. Omit it to return to the
previous release.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

pattern.description: Pattern is the URL pattern to bind, e.g. "acme.com/api/*".

script.description:
Script is the Worker script to dispatch to. Omit it to leave the pattern
bound to no script, which is how Cloudflare expresses "bypass the Worker here".

zone.description: Zone is the 32-hex Cloudflare zone id, from the path.

action.description: Action is the name of the connector action to invoke.

auth.description:
Auth is the caller's resolved credential for the connector, handed to the
action verbatim. Its shape is whatever the connector's auth descriptor
declares (a token string, an object), so it is opaque here.

id.description: ID is the connector to run, from the path.

props.description: Props are the action's input properties, keyed by property name.

env.description:
Env is the run's environment. Keys must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`;
a variable marked `secret: true` is sealed into KMS.

gpu.description: GPU is how many GPUs the run asks for; a negative value is 400.

image.description: Image is the container image to run. Required.

maxScale.description:
MaxScale above the floor declares an autoscaling ceiling; 0 means no
autoscaler at all — a fixed run at the floor.

minScale.description: MinScale is the replica floor, clamped to the deployment's limit.

name.description:
Name is the run's name, and the slug is derived from it. Required, and it
must resolve to `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$`. Re-running the same
name updates that run in place.

port.description: Port is the container port the run listens on.

runtime.description:
Runtime is accepted for the client contract and echoed nowhere: the image
IS the runtime unit.

shape.description:
Shape is a compute size label, echoed back; sizing is the operator's
default. Defaults to "auto".

arch.description: Arch is the target architecture for the artifact lane.

binaries.description:
Binaries selects the ARTIFACT lane (artifact.go): build what the repo's
hanzo.yml `binaries:` block declares — a Go binary, an npm tarball, a Rust
binary — and publish it to hanzoai/s3 instead of pushing an image. It is the
same recipe hanzoai/ci reads, sent verbatim, so `image` is meaningless here
and must be absent.

branch.description: Branch is the branch to build when no SHA or Ref is given.

bucket.description: Bucket mirrors hanzo.yml's `bucket:` — where the artifact lane publishes.

context.description: Context is the build context path within the repo.

dockerTarget.description: DockerTarget is the multi-stage build target to stop at.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile is the path to build from; empty uses the zero-config frontend.

image.description:
Image is the output image ref to push. Required on the image lane, and it
must target a registry namespace the caller's org owns.

organizationId.description:
OrgID attributes the build to an org. On the IAM path it defaults to the
caller's own validated org, and a foreign one is refused unless the caller
is a platform SuperAdmin.

os.description: OS is the target operating system for the artifact lane.

ref.description: Ref is the git ref to build when no SHA is given.

release.description:
Release requests native release semantics for cloud's self-publish: compute
the next version, build+push ghcr.io/hanzoai/cloud, smoke it, then tag (the
receipt) and notify universe. It owns its output image (release.go), and it
takes SuperAdmin.

repo.description: Repo is the repository clone URL to build. Required on the image lane.

sha.description: SHA is the commit to pin; it wins over Ref and Branch.

tag.description:
Tag is the publish path segment, so both front doors write ONE index at ONE
URL. It defaults to the pinned ref, and must be named explicitly for a
branch.

documentIds.description: DocumentIDs are data room document ids to raise a signature request over. Required.

signers.description: Signers are the recipients, each a name and an email. Required.

chainId.description:
ChainID is the EVM chain the Safe transaction is bound to. 0 uses the
wallet's own chain, or the Hanzo L1 (36963) when it is chain-agnostic.

data.description: Data is the call data, hex-encoded.

nonce.description: Nonce is the Safe's transaction nonce.

to.description: To is the transaction's target address.

value.description: Value is the native-token amount to send, as a decimal string in wei.

gpuUtil.description:
GPUUtil is accelerator utilization as a fraction 0..1; the warehouse clamps
anything outside that.

gpus.description:
GPUs is how many accelerators the reading covers, GPUModel the representative
model name.

host.description: Host is the node's hostname, for display.

memUsed.description: MemUsed and MemFree are host memory in bytes.

unit.description:
Unit is the reporting node's own id — the same id it registered under, and
the key the board joins this series onto. Required.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description:
ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339. Empty is
allowed; anything else that is not RFC3339 is refused.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. Empty is allowed;
anything else that is not RFC3339 is refused.

doctypes.description:
DocTypes restricts retrieval to a subset of the indexed knowledge doctypes
(kb-page, kb-memory, kb-source). An empty or foreign list reads all of them.

limit.description: Limit bounds the hits returned. Default 10, maximum 50.

project.description: Project narrows retrieval to one project scope.

query.description: Query is the natural-language question. Required.

amountCents.description: AmountCents is the capital to inject, in minor units. Must be > 0.

memo.description: Memo is the operator's note on the entry. Empty takes "reserve capital injection".

ref.description: Ref is an idempotency key. Without one each seed is a distinct injection.

service.description: Service is the slug to flip, taken from the path.

waitlistMode.description:
WaitlistMode is the new mode: true gates the service behind the waitlist, false
opens it. This is the launch lever.

betaOrgs.description:
BetaOrgs REPLACES the item's beta grant list when present. Omit it to
leave the existing grants alone.

id.description:
ID is the item within that namespace — a model id, a provider name, or a
feature's key.

kind.description: Kind is the item's namespace: "model", "provider" or "feature".

state.description:
State is the item's global enablement: "off" (hidden from everyone,
absolutely), "beta" (visible only to granted orgs) or "ga" (visible to
everyone). Required.

app.description: App is the application's slug, from the path.

env.description:
Env is the app's whole environment set, REPLACING what it had. Keys must
match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`; a variable marked `secret: true` is
sealed into KMS and blanked in the database.

project.description: Project is the project the application lives under, from the path.

active.description: Active is the switch itself: true enables the flag for every evaluation.

filters.description:
Filters is the optional rollout/payload block of a VALUED switch, e.g.
{"groups":[{"properties":[],"rollout_percentage":100}],"payloads":{"true":250}}.

key.description: Key is the switch to write, taken from the path (e.g. "waitlist.chat").

config.description:
Config is the product's non-secret configuration, stored verbatim. Bounded at
64 KiB once serialized. Omit it to store an empty object.

product.description:
Product is the catalog slug, from the PATH. zip binds the path last, so the
URL names the product being written whatever a body field claims.

secrets.description:
Secrets are the secret fields, by name. Each VALUE is sealed into KMS and
never reaches this deployment's database; a value that is empty or equal to
the mask the read path returns means "unchanged" and is skipped, so a console
round-trip cannot blank a stored secret. A key must match
^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$, a value is bounded at 8 KiB, and an org may hold
at most 64 secret fields per product.

digest.description:
Digest is a pre-computed 32-byte digest as hex, with or without the 0x
prefix. When present it is signed verbatim and message is ignored.

message.description:
Message is arbitrary text to hash with Keccak256 and sign. Used only when
digest is empty.

id.description: ID is the document to send for signature, from the path.

signers.description:
Signers are the people who must sign, by name and email. At least one is
required.

content.description: Content is the SKILL.md body. Required, at most 256 KiB.

description.description: Description is the one-line summary discovery shows for the skill.

name.description:
Name is the skill's id within the org: one lowercase path segment
(a-z0-9, _ or -). Writing an existing name REVISES that skill.

stream.description: Stream is the stream to update, from the path.

name.description: Name is the stream's name within the org: 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

enabled.description:
Enabled publishes the script on <script>.<subdomain>.workers.dev when true,
and withdraws it when false.

script.description: Script is the Worker script name, from the path.

email.description: Email is the subject's contact email, sealed at rest.

kind.description: Kind is the party type: "individual" (KYC) or "business" (KYB).

name.description: Name is the subject's name, sealed at rest.

ref.description: Ref is the org's own opaque external id for this subject.

channel.description:
Channel is the Slack channel the notifier posts to — an id (C…/G…), a
#name, or a bare name. Required.

events.description:
Events narrows delivery to these lifecycle kinds (push.landed,
deploy.live, deploy.failed). Omit it to receive every deliverable kind; a
kind that is never posted to Slack is refused rather than silently dropped.

name.description: Name is the repo to subscribe, from the :name path segment.

period.description: Period is the accrual period as YYYY-MM. Empty takes the current UTC month.

revenueCents.description: RevenueCents is the net platform revenue measured for the period, in minor units. Must be >= 0.

actor.description:
Actor is the identity the sync writes as, used as the loop guard so its own
writes do not re-trigger it. Defaults to the deployment's GIT_SYNC_ACTOR.

direction.description: Direction is both (the default), pull, push or off.

kind.description: Kind is what is being synced. Only "git" today, which is also the default.

run.description: Run reconciles once immediately after the upsert, in the background.

source.description: Source is the upstream end. Required.

target.description:
Target is the downstream end. Optional for git: a native repository named
after the source is derived when it is omitted.

trigger.description: Trigger is what starts a reconcile: webhook (the default), poll or manual.

body.description:
Body is the text/template source. Required. Every {{.key}} it references must
be declared in Fields, or the save is refused rather than rendering a blank
into a contract later.

category.description:
Category groups the template: formation, equity, ops or sales. Optional when
overriding a built-in, which supplies its own.

counselReview.description:
CounselReview marks a template whose documents must carry the counsel notice.
It can be raised but never lowered: a formation or equity template is always
counsel-review, and an override of a counsel-review built-in stays one.

fields.description:
Fields declares the merge fields the body consumes. Every declared field is
REQUIRED at generation — the engine fails closed on a missing one.

id.description:
ID is the template to override, from the path. Overriding a built-in id
inherits that built-in's category, title and counsel-review posture.

title.description: Title is the template's display name. Required unless a built-in supplies it.

arguments.description:
Arguments is the tool's own input object, passed through verbatim to
whichever source owns it.

name.description: Name is the tool to run, exactly as GET /v1/tools reports it.

doctype.description: DocType is the content type to act on, from the path.

name.description: Name is the document to act on, from the path.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is an ISO-8601 go-live time handed to the channel's own scheduler;
"" distributes now.

to.description:
To is the lifecycle state to move to. Required, and the move must be a legal
edge from the item's current state.

ref.description: Ref is the agent to update — its public id or org-unique name, from the path.

account.description: Account is the provider ad-account this campaign runs on (Meta act_<id>). Optional.

budget.description: Budget is the campaign budget in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

name.description: Name is the campaign's display label. Required; trimmed and bounded to 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the campaign goal as the provider names it. Optional, bounded to 1024 bytes.

platform.description: Platform is the ad network: meta, google, tiktok or x. Empty defaults to meta.

spend.description: Spend is the amount spent so far in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

status.description: Status is the lifecycle state: draft, active, paused or completed. Empty defaults to draft.

description.description: Description is a free-text label for the console. Optional, clipped to 1024 bytes.

events.description:
Events are NATS subject patterns to subscribe to. An empty or omitted list
means EVERY event. Max 64 patterns, each max 256 bytes.

status.description: Status is "active" or "disabled". Empty defaults to active.

url.description:
URL is the https:// address each matching event is POSTed to. Required,
max 2048 bytes; http:// and every other scheme is refused.

handle.description:
Handle is the display name shown on a listed row: 1-40 characters of letters,
digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a listing
opt-in it defaults to the caller's username.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the caller's row to other viewers of the board when true, and
anonymizes it when false.

nonce.description: Nonce is the value GET /v1/validators/challenge issued for this slot.

signature.description:
Signature is the wallet's personal_sign over the challenge message, hex with
a 0x prefix.

tokenId.description:
TokenID is the Validator-tier GenesisNFT token id being claimed. It IS the
validator slot.

clientId.description: ClientID is the Azure AD application id. Azure only.

clientSecret.description:
ClientSecret selects the service-principal flow. LEAVING IT OUT selects
keyless workload identity federation instead, so omitting it is a choice
rather than an omission. Azure only.

credentialJson.description:
CredentialJSON is a Google credentials document — an external_account
(workload identity federation, keyless) or a service-account key. GCP only.

externalId.description:
ExternalID pins that role assumption to Hanzo, which is what closes the
confused-deputy hole. AWS only.

label.description:
Label is the org-chosen name for this account within the provider, which is
how a second account at the same provider is addressed later. Empty means
"default"; anything outside 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9._-] is refused.

projectIds.description: ProjectIDs bounds the GKE cluster sweep. GCP only.

provider.description:
Provider is the cloud being linked, from the path: digitalocean, aws, gcp
or azure.

regions.description: Regions bounds the AWS EKS cluster sweep. AWS only.

roleArn.description:
RoleARN is the AWS role Hanzo assumes into the account — the keyless path,
so no access key is ever stored.

subscriptionIds.description: SubscriptionIDs bounds the AKS cluster sweep. Azure only.

tenantId.description: TenantID is the Azure AD tenant of the app. Azure only.

token.description:
Token is the DigitalOcean personal access token. DigitalOcean only, and it
is the one provider that requires storing a secret.

id.description: ID is the verification to decide, from the path.

status.description:
Status is the reviewer's decision: "reviewer_confirmed" (a pass) or
"manual_review" (withheld for review) — never a provider status.

email.description: Email is an inline subject's contact email, sealed at rest.

kind.description: Kind is an inline subject's party type: "individual" (KYC) or "business" (KYB).

name.description: Name is an inline subject's name, sealed at rest.

ref.description: Ref is the org's own opaque external id for an inline subject.

subjectId.description: SubjectID names an existing subject to verify; empty creates one inline.

repoUrl.description:
RepoURL is what to claim: a repository (github.com/owner/name) or a whole
OWNER (github.com/owner, no repository segment). gitlab.com is accepted too.

email.description: Email identifies the entry to boost. Either this or RefCode is required.

points.description:
Points is how many points to award. Must be positive — this seam exists to move
someone UP toward the cutoff.

reason.description:
Reason is the operator's justification. Not sent to the engine; it is recorded on
the audit row, which is the point of asking for it.

refCode.description: RefCode identifies the entry by its referral code, when the email is unknown.

waitlist.description: Waitlist is the waitlist slug the grant lands on. Required.

get.summary: Lists every affiliate across the fleet with its ORG exposed, plus a fleet summary of lifetime accrued, still-pending and paid commission in integer cents.

post.summary: Runs the accrual: for each referred org it reads that org's metered spend for the current period and accrues commission to every affiliate up its referral chain, then answers how many sources were swept and how many NEW accruals landed.

parameters.description: ID is the affiliate to approve, from the path.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Approves an affiliate and MINTS its referral code — the moment the partner has a working share link and starts accruing.

parameters.description: ID is the affiliate to pay, from the path.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Pays out accrued commission and answers the payout row with the affiliate's updated balances.

parameters.description: ID is the affiliate whose direct rate moves, from the path.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Sets one affiliate's DIRECT commission rate, in basis points of Hanzo's margin.

parameters.description: ID is the affiliate's server-minted handle, "aff_"-prefixed.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Suspends an affiliate: it stops accruing on the next sweep, and its code stops resolving for new attributions.

parameters.description:

parameters.name: range

get.summary: Is the fleet AI board: LLM generations over gen_ai spans (count, cost, avg/p95 latency, per-model), per-model usage from the live cloud_usage ledger, and the eval plane (traces, scores, score names, runs, and the average-score trend).

parameters.description:
Range is the lower time bound: 24h, 7d or 30d. Anything else reads as the
board's own default.
parameters.name: range

get.summary: Is the SaaS product-analytics board over the caller's tenant window: active customers, new and churned, retention, MRR, ARPU, the usage trend and the top customers by spend — every number folded from the commerce ledger, not sampled.

Owner is the org whose rows to read. Defaults to the admin org, which owns the
platform's roles and applications.
parameters.name: owner

parameters.description:

default otherwise.
parameters.name: p

parameters.description: PageSize is rows per page. Forwarded only when set.
parameters.name: pageSize

get.summary: Lists IAM applications for one owner org, forwarded VERBATIM from IAM's get-applications.

parameters.name: org

parameters.name: sub

parameters.description: Action restricts it to one action name, e.g. "admin.waitlist.grant".
parameters.name: action

parameters.description: Resource restricts it to one resource kind, e.g. "credit-grant".

parameters.description:
Since is the inclusive lower time bound, RFC3339. An unparseable value is

parameters.name: since

parameters.name: until

get.summary: Reads cloud's tamper-evident audit trail, newest first, with the chain's live integrity attached so a listing can be badged as verified.

Walks the WHOLE hash chain and reports whether it is intact: how many records were checked, the head hash to pin externally against tail-truncation, and — when the chain is broken — the seq of the first bad record and why.

parameters.description:
Limit bounds the page. 0 or less means the default of 500; anything above
1000 is clamped to 1000.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Returns the platform's whole author program — every org's author record, not the caller's — with each one's repository and deploy counts and a fleet roll-up of the money accrued, pending and paid.

post.summary: Runs the accrual sweep across every approved author: for each of their deploying orgs it computes this period's royalty from that org's metered spend and latches it at most once per period.

parameters.name: id

post.summary: Admits one author to EARNING, optionally on a negotiated royalty share.

Period is the UTC accrual month, YYYY-MM. Empty means every period; any other
shape is refused with 400.

get.summary: Returns the audit trail behind ONE author's royalty — the same payload the author reads at /v1/authors/basis, from the same builder, so support sees exactly what the author sees rather than a parallel view free to drift.

parameters.name: id

post.summary: Records a payout of accrued royalty and settles it.

parameters.description: ID is the author record's handle, "aut_"-prefixed.

Kind narrows to one workload class (bot | machine | cluster | nodepool |
container | function | …). An OPEN spectrum matched as a plain string, lowercased
to the warehouse's convention; empty means every kind.

Org narrows to one tenant. Empty means every tenant — this board is
cross-tenant by nature.

parameters.name: range

Lists every customer org at a glance, sorted by slug: owner email, plan, suspend status, member count, balance, month-to-date spend and MRR.

parameters.description: Org is the tenant slug from the path.

within a cluster, and an operator reads the name off the board.

droplet down again, so it defaults false — a CPU/RAM-only change, reversible.
